summary: macOS local peer attribution now walks proc_pidinfo ancestry and KERN_PROCARGS2 environments with nearest-process masking and before/after process-birth validation. A successful walk without a harness remains a person; failed inspection cannot grant person authority.

compatibility.detail: No wire shape change. On Linux and macOS, present but empty, conflicting or invalid agent identity values and unsuccessful process inspection are unverifiable, not person callers. Failed local peer inspection denies backup/proof exports, internal routes, LOCAL_PERSON_HEADER sessions and actor/requester body impersonation, rather than all public traffic. Ancestry must match the accept-time connector generation before and after inspection; failed capture is unverifiable. macOS has no pidfd: before/after birth-time checks narrow but cannot eliminate the PID reuse window. Ancestry binding prevents accidental impersonation by cooperative agents; it is not a boundary against deliberate evasion. See schickling/dotfiles#8659.

downtime.detail: Takes effect after daemon restart with the new build.

recovery.detail: Revert the commit and restart the daemon.
